Question ID: ALG1_U01_L02_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

Which number is less: -8 or -3? Number line reference: -8 ... -3 ... 0. Values farther left are less.

feedback.text: This confuses larger absolute value with greater value. For negative numbers, the number farther left is less.
On a number line, -8 is farther left than -3, so -8 is less.
This ignores the negative signs. The question compares -8 and -3, not positive 3.
This changes the sign and does not answer the comparison between the two given numbers.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U01_L02_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

Evaluate -6 + 14. Number line movement: start at -6, move 14 units right, end at 8.

feedback.text: This adds the absolute values and keeps the result positive without considering opposite signs.
This adds the absolute values and keeps a negative sign, but the positive value has the larger absolute value.
This subtracts correctly but uses the wrong sign. Since 14 is farther from zero than -6, the result is positive.
The signs are different, so subtract 14 - 6 = 8. The positive number has the larger absolute value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U01_L02_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

Evaluate 5 - (-9). Number line movement: subtracting -9 means add 9, so start at 5 and move 9 units right.

feedback.text: This treats subtraction of a negative as ordinary subtraction. Subtracting a negative means adding the opposite.
This subtracts 5 from 9 and misses the meaning of subtracting a negative.
This uses the correct distance but the wrong sign. Adding 9 to 5 gives a positive result.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U01_L02_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

Evaluate (-4)(-7). Sign-rule table: same signs make a positive product; different signs make a negative product.

feedback.text: This multiplies correctly but uses the wrong sign. Same signs make a positive product.
This adds the numbers instead of multiplying them.
A negative times a negative is positive, and 4 times 7 = 28.
This uses addition reasoning instead of multiplication reasoning.

Question ID: ALG1_U01_L02_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only - No primary MLA standard assigned in approved mapping

Evaluate -1/2 + 3/4. Fraction reference: -1/2 is the same as -2/4, so combine -2/4 and 3/4.

feedback.text: This subtracts correctly but keeps the wrong sign. The positive fraction has the larger value.
This adds the absolute values instead of combining opposite-signed rational numbers.
This adds the absolute values and keeps a negative sign, but the signs are different.
